finding: onSubscriptionAttemptFailed reports only on `subscriptionFailures === SUBSCRIPTION_FAILURE_LIMIT` (strict equality) and the counter resets ONLY on a successful PUT or stop(). Under a permanently-failing subscription it climbs to 4,5,6... and ==3 is never true again. sendMessage sets `error:null, isStreaming:true` at the start of every turn, so the SECOND turn reverts to the exact infinite spinner this branch exists to remove. INV-4 held for exactly one occurrence per page load.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / re-arm on >= LIMIT with a re-report interval

finding: Same one-shot defect, reached independently: INV-4 ("a realtime delivery failure must not present as still working") is contradicted by the shipped code on the second user interaction. Also notes the test `reports at most ONCE per failure run` LOCKS the defect in — a test written against the implementation rather than the promise.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1

finding: The action applies buildSendFailureState unconditionally, which always sets `lastTurnInterrupted: true`. MessageList renders that as an `interrupted` badge on the last assistant message. In the PRIMARY trigger path (subscription fails at conversation open, no turn in flight) it decorates a fully-persisted, completed reply as interrupted.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / only apply the turn reset when a turn is actually in flight

finding: The single user-facing string is unconditional: 'The reply is still being generated and saved — reload to see it.' In the open-conversation path there is no reply being generated, so the one message this invariant produces is false in its most common trigger.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / message chosen by whether a turn is in flight

finding: `set(existing ? {...patch, error: existing} : patch)` keeps a stale earlier error and DROPS the live-updates message. Combined with the one-shot report above, the user is then never told the real ongoing problem. The third store test locks this in rather than catching it.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / the delivery failure is the more actionable error and now wins

finding: The `?? 0` tail materialises a fully-populated progress_data for a row that previously had NONE. DownloadItem.renderProgressInfo() returns null when progress_data is absent, so a queued download that used to render no byte line now renders the literal '0 Bytes / 0 Bytes' until the first real tick — re-introducing the reported symptom string in a different state, and contradicting this function's own doc comment ("a null means unknown, never zero").
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / keep progress_data undefined when nothing is known

finding: `error_message: update.error_message ?? download.error_message` makes a server-side CLEAR of the error un-observable: the repository sets error_message unconditionally, so a null on the wire genuinely means cleared, but the row keeps stale red error text. Same for model_id. These fields carry the whole row's value, unlike the progress figures, so the fallback semantics were wrong for them.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1

finding: DOWNLOAD_STATUSES is a hand-respelled mirror of the generated DownloadStatus union. Adding a server status is not a type error against `readonly DownloadStatus[]`, and narrowStatus then silently keeps the previous status, so a new terminal status would leave the row permanently 'downloading' and never filtered out. This is the same drift class the branch's own comments condemn for the CORS header.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / exhaustive Record<DownloadStatus, true> so a new variant is a compile error

finding: create_cors_layer_with is pub and takes &[&str]; nothing in the type system stops a future caller passing a config-derived slice, which would reintroduce operator-injected header names into the allow-list. No exposure today (both callers pass consts).
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / signature narrowed to &'static [&'static str]

finding: The fix relocates the remembering from N config files to ONE Rust const; it does not eliminate it. Nothing connects REQUIRED_CUSTOM_REQUEST_HEADERS to the headers the client actually sends, and `the_required_list_is_sourced_from_the_handler_constants` cannot fail when a FOURTH header is added and forgotten. The design's framing ("the failure was not that someone forgot a string") is overstated relative to what shipped.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / design doc + code comment narrowed to the claim that is actually true; a source-scanning guard deliberately NOT added (that guard class has failed to converge twice in this repo)

finding: `the_required_list_is_sourced_from_the_handler_constants` compares &str VALUES, so replacing the constant reference with an equal literal leaves it green. It detects a drift in spelling (already covered by the preflight test), not a drift in sourcing, despite its doc claiming the opposite.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / renamed + comment corrected to what it actually pins

finding: The timing assertion stamps time when the TEST TASK dequeues from the probe's unbounded channel, not when the frame arrived. On the documented shared/contended box a >240ms deschedule after the send would leave both frames already queued, `lead` microseconds, and the assertion fails on a perfectly incremental server.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / pacing widened to 400ms, threshold 150ms, limitation documented in the test

finding: This file names itself INV-2's acceptance test and then admits reqwest performs no preflight, so it passed while the desktop app was completely broken. Deleting the whole fix leaves all three green. INV-2 therefore has a correct fix and no single test that can fail on the promise.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / INV-2's acceptance is now explicitly the CONJUNCTION of the preflight tests and this one, stated in TESTS.md; the e2e also now asserts the browser really issues and completes the subscription PUT

finding: The design's own causal chain names `reloadOpen` bailing while isStreaming as why the pane cannot self-heal, and the fix leaves it untouched. A mid-turn stream drop that loses the `complete` frame reproduces the identical wedge and reports nothing (the post-reconnect PUT succeeds, resetting the counter). The Out-of-scope section carves out only UPSTREAM stalls, so this is silently dropped rather than deferred.
resolution: Pre-existing self-heal hole, not introduced here; changing reloadOpen's isStreaming guard risks clobbering a live buffer, which is what that guard exists to prevent. Now recorded EXPLICITLY in the design's Out of scope with this reasoning, and escalated to the lead rather than left implicit.

finding: Routing the catch onto the abort-and-reconnect path means a transient PUT rejection now tears down a healthy live stream and waits out the backoff, where previously it was ignored. Self-heals via replay, so churn rather than data loss.
resolution: This is DEC-3, taken deliberately and argued there: silence is what produced the reported bug, the pre-existing non-2xx branch already did exactly this, and the cost is bounded by the existing exponential backoff. Kept, with the auditor's sharper framing folded into DEC-3.

finding: set_subscription returns 204 even for a connection id the registry does not know (`let Some(conn) = ... else { return; }`), so an ineffective subscription resets the client's failure counter. 'The PUT succeeded' is not evidence the connection is subscribed.
resolution: Real, and pre-existing. Fixing it changes a documented response code (a contract change needing an OpenAPI regen in both workspaces) for a self-limiting race. Escalated to the lead as a follow-up rather than widened into this branch.

finding: set_subscription verifies CONVERSATION ownership but never that conn_id belongs to auth.user.id. An authenticated user who learned another user's connection UUID could re-point that connection (victim's stream goes silent). Requires guessing a UUIDv4 delivered only over the victim's own authenticated stream.
resolution: Pre-existing; adjacent because this branch makes the endpoint reachable in more deployment shapes. Escalated to the lead — binding conn->user is the right fix and belongs in its own reviewed change.

finding: SSE_CLIENTS is a process-global pool and broadcast_event fans EVERY active download to EVERY subscriber; the only gate is the LlmModelsDownloadsRead permission, so a user holding it sees other users' download rows.
resolution: Pre-existing cross-user visibility, untouched by this branch (which only adds KeepAlive here). Genuinely worth fixing; escalated to the lead as the most substantive pre-existing finding this audit surfaced.

finding: An allow_headers list whose every entry fails HeaderName parsing collapses to headers.is_empty() -> Any. Fails OPEN, silently: an operator typo ('Content Type') turns an intended allow-list into a wildcard.
resolution: Pre-existing and deliberately preserved byte-for-byte by this change (config_headers_are_any is computed from the config list alone, precisely to avoid altering it). Changing fail-open to fail-closed is a behaviour change for every deployment and belongs in its own change. Escalated.

finding: http://localhost:1420 (the dev Vite origin) is in the desktop allow-list unconditionally, including release builds, so any local process able to bind 1420 gets an allowlisted origin against the embedded API.
resolution: Pre-existing, moved verbatim by the extraction (origins and methods are byte-identical, confirmed by the auditor). Gating it on debug_assertions is a real improvement but changes desktop behaviour beyond this branch's scope. Escalated.

finding: The relocated doc comment asserts the ngrok tunnel origin is 'added at tunnel-start time'. There is no such code: allow_origins has exactly one non-test producer, this function. The claim was equally wrong before the move, but the diff re-authored it as the function's contract.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / claim corrected

finding: The heading '## Out of scope (recorded, not fixed)' contradicts its own second bullet, which ends 'Only the missing KeepAlive is fixed here' — and it IS fixed. A reader scanning headings gets the wrong answer.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / heading + bullet restructured

finding: SUBSCRIPTION_FAILURE_LIMIT = 3 (~7s to banner) is a user-visible policy the design never states: an ordinary transient blip lasting three attempts raises an error banner and terminates the turn's UI state.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / stated in the design doc and in DEC-4

finding: 'This drives the REAL client path ... Only the two endpoints are served from fixtures' overstates it — those two endpoints ARE the entire server side of the feature, and the SSE frame is hand-authored in the spec. The repo's CODING_GUIDELINES §14 also says 'No page.route() API mocking' for e2e, so both new specs are exceptions that deserve an explicit note.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / claim narrowed, the §14 exception named and justified in both specs

finding: 'never renders a blank alert' exercises buildSendFailureState's pre-existing fallback with an input the production caller cannot produce; it is not evidence about the new action. Similarly `const _SUBSCRIPTION_HEADER` in the incremental test is inert decoration.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / reframed to pin the property that matters (the action cannot produce a blank banner because it routes through the shared builder); the inert const removed

finding: An update for an id not already in state.downloads is discarded and no row is created, so a download started on another tab/device renders nothing. Pre-existing and outside the diff, but the design states INV-3 unconditionally.
resolution: Pre-existing; creating rows from SSE frames would need the full DownloadInstance the wire event does not carry (request_data.display_name and friends), so it is a real feature, not a patch. Recorded in the design's Out of scope and escalated.

finding: desktop_cors_config_lists_both_connection_id_headers re-spells the literal it checks, and the sibling preflight test passes with the list entry removed — so by this branch's own stated criterion it is a tautology. (Self-disclosed in its doc comment.)
resolution: Kept deliberately and the comment already says why: after the union the desktop list is documentation, and this pins that the documentation stays true. Reframed in FIX_ROUND-1 so it no longer reads as a second proof of the same property.

finding: an_unsubscribed_connection_is_the_broken_case duplicates the pre-existing chat_stream_test.rs::unsubscribed_connection_receives_nothing, adding only the persistence assertion.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / now cites the sibling and states that the persistence half is what it adds

finding: The comment says cross-origin cookie mode 'additionally requires allow_credentials + explicit (non-"*") origins', but CorsConfig cannot express allow_credentials and nothing in the tree sets it. An operator following the comment builds a deployment that cannot work.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 / comment corrected in both examples
